source.title: Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures
source.authors: Aditi Khandelwal; A. Tarun; Yi-Xuan Xu; Imanol Schlag; Golnoosh Farnadi; Siva Reddy; Luke S. Zettlemoyer; Antoine Bosselut

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-law claims in a new setting: text, vision, and audio multimodal MoE pretraining, including repeated data and continual pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fitted validation-loss scaling exponents, compute-optimal allocations, and held-out predictions. It also reports repetition and fitting-span results relevant to the scope and fit dependence of those laws. Comparisons to scaling results from cited prior work are not recorded as independent results.
record.test_reason: The study fits Chinchilla-form validation-loss laws for text, vision and audio in multimodal MoE pretraining. It derives compute-optimal splits, predicts held-out from-scratch and continual-pretraining runs, and reports how extrapolation error and coefficients change with the fitting span. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a repetition-aware, mixture-dependent extension of the Chinchilla law fits multimodal MoE losses. They find compute-optimal allocation is modality-specific (text and vision balanced, audio model-heavy), non-text repetition saturates after about 2 epochs, and cross-modal transfer is asymmetric. They report that the law predicts held-out runs (8 of 9 within 2.6%). They frame it as a framework for context-specific laws, not universal coefficients.
record.recipe_differences: Extends the standard Chinchilla form with mixture-dependent effective capacity, directional cross-modal transfer, and repetition saturation; jointly fits modality-specific parameters using Huber loss on log validation loss and L-BFGS.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that coefficients may depend on tokenizers, loss objective, MoE architectural hyperparameters, and dataset quality. Extrapolation accuracy also varies with the range of model scales included in fitting. Audio-source transfer coefficients are unstable across leave-one-scale-out folds and random-subset refits.

fits_no_version.finding: Directional cross-modal transfer coefficients (e.g. v_vision→audio = −0.795) and capacity-dilution coefficients (c_audio = −1.87) for MoE modality mixtures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multimodal MoE pretraining, co-trained modalities change a target modality's effective data and capacity in an asymmetric, fittable way.

record.problems: The fitted experiments use six model scales from 457M to 8.3B total parameters and a single seed for most runs; seed checks cover only the smallest and largest models for 30B tokens. The authors state that validation at substantially larger scales (≫ 10B active parameters, > 1T tokens) is future work and that fitted coefficients may depend on setup choices. One CPT text prediction has 6.73% relative error.

untested.parts: Several orders of magnitude: parameters span only 457M-8.3B (about 1.3 decades) and text tokens 10B-100B (1 decade). Dense models and compute as the scaling variable are not tested.

Prediction of runs orders of magnitude larger: the held-out from-scratch run is about 1.5× the largest fitted model, and the authors leave validation beyond 10B active parameters and 1T tokens to future work.
Stability of the optimal N/D exponents across compute budgets: no IsoFLOP or direct compute-optimal runs; the split is induced from α and β.
All of it: depth is fixed at 32 layers and only d_model varies.
Image and video models outside this MoE early-fusion setup, fine-tuning, and transfer.
All of it: no downstream task results.
Parameter counting, training schedule, tokenizer and objective are not varied (the authors only speculate about tokenizer and objective). Curvature away from a single power law is not examined.

missing.what: Fitted exponents vary strongly with fitting span, e.g. αAudio 4.252 (M1-M2 fit) against 0.324 joint, and αVision 0.334-1.100.
Leave-one-scale-out interpolation: held-out maximum relative error ≤2.31%, with stable base exponents (αText 0.359 ± 0.012).
Component ablations: removing the repetition term raises RMSE_log by 49.4%, and dropping components worsens extrapolation from M1-M2 (up to 10.55%).
Random 90% subset refits: base exponents recovered (e.g. βText 0.401 ± 0.062 against 0.337 joint).

record.verdict_notes: Vision α is inconsistent: 0.50 in Table 1 against 0.568 in the Table 4-6 joint fits. Table 10's caption says within 2.51%, the text says 2.6%. Table 2 totals exclude embeddings, while model names include them. The main from-scratch held-out test is only about 1.5× in scale, so the V2 support covers short-range extrapolation only. Vision and audio losses include text-token loss. Most runs use a single seed.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments concern multimodal MoEs and their stated data and training setup, not language models across all architectures or training regimes.

The largest from-scratch validation model is 12.6B total parameters and 200B tokens; the CPT tests use an 8.3B model. The paper notes that validation at substantially larger scales (≫ 10B active parameters, > 1T tokens) remains future work.
The compute-optimal exponents are induced from fitted exponents assuming C ∝ N × D, and are specific to the tested modality and setup.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.

The study tests text, vision, and audio in its MoE setup, including repeated non-text data and CPT; it does not test image/video models generally, other modalities such as long-form video, or fine-tuning and transfer broadly.
The study reports modality-specific validation losses, not downstream task performance or its predictability.
It does not systematically vary tokenizers, objectives, architectures, or data quality to measure their effects, and does not establish that curves generally bend away from a single power law.
